claims.text: Helm installs resources in a fixed order by Kubernetes kind, defined in kind_sorter.go in the Helm repo; chart authors can't declare dependencies between resources or subcharts except through hook weights.
In Pulumi, resource ordering derives from the dependency graph: each resource waits for its dependencies to become ready and independent resources deploy in parallel.
The Helm docs state: "the Kubernetes objects from the charts and all its dependencies are aggregated into a single set; then sorted by type followed by name; and then created/updated in that order."

Helm's kind sorter is a hardcoded list beginning with PriorityClasses and Namespaces, then Secrets and ConfigMaps, then CustomResourceDefinitions and RBAC, then Services and workloads, with unlisted kinds (including custom resources) last.
Helm uninstall runs the same kind-sorted list in reverse.
Helm sends sorted manifests to the API server in a single pass and doesn't wait for one resource to become ready before applying the next.
A Helm subchart's objects are merged into the parent chart's set and sorted by kind, so a chart can't express installing one subchart before another.
Helm chart hooks are ordered with helm.sh/hook-weight annotations, and hook resources are not managed by Helm as part of the release.
HIP-0025 proposes native sequencing for resources and subcharts in Helm and is still a draft.
Passing one resource's output into another, or setting the dependsOn resource option, creates an edge in the Pulumi dependency graph.
Pulumi deletes follow the dependency graph in reverse.

The Pulumi Kubernetes provider's helm.v4.Chart supports the config.kubernetes.io/depends-on annotation for ordering between objects inside the chart, and dependsOn on the chart for dependencies on outside resources.
Helm merges objects from a chart and its dependencies into a single set, sorts by Kubernetes kind and applies in that order, so declaring a subchart as a dependency doesn't make it install first.
Two patterns cover most production deployments of Pulumi and Helm together.
Using Helm charts directly from a Pulumi program is the most common adoption pattern.
helm.v4.Chart registers each chart object as a Pulumi resource so every child shows up in plan output, drift detection, and state.
helm.v3.Release uses the embedded Helm SDK and creates a real Helm release, preserving chart hooks, post-rendering, and release history.
Pulumi installs a Helm chart after the resources its values depend on.
Helm is a graduated CNCF project, open source under Apache License 2.0, with no commercial tier.
A failed Pulumi update leaves the stack partially updated, and you roll forward by reverting program code and running pulumi up.
Pulumi creates and deletes resources in dependency order, with each resource ready before dependents.
